# Todoist — Style Reference

> Warm brown ink thinned on oat paper, one tomato on the desk. Graphik semibold headlines and medium-weight Inter sit on #fefdfc linen, ruled by 18%-alpha ink hairlines, with a single #e34432 tomato button.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Todoist speaks a diluted-ink product language: every neutral on the page is the same warm brown-black #25221e at a different opacity rather than a stepped gray ramp. The canvas is #fefdfc linen, recessed tiles drop to #f9f7f6, floating menus and product windows lift to #ffffff, and the dark secondary button is the same ink at 83% alpha (#25221ed4). The chromatic budget is one saturated hue. Tomato #e34432 is permitted on the primary action and nowhere else in the UI. Three pastel washes (#f4fbf7, #f6faeb, #fff6f0) and per-section eyebrow tints are atmosphere, not signal. Type carries hierarchy through family and size, not weight. Graphik at 600 handles 22–55px headlines with -0.01em tracking, and Inter at 500 handles everything else with +0.01em tracking. The body-to-display jump is 3.5×, with no ladder between them. Shapes are soft-rounded (8px controls, 15px cards). Elevation is rationed to three warm-tinted shadows. The result reads as a calm notebook rather than a productivity dashboard.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Linen Canvas | `#fefdfc` | `--color-linen-canvas` | Page background behind the hero, feature blocks and footer. A barely warm off-white that keeps the alpha-ink text from turning cold, as a pure #ffffff canvas would. |
| Paper White | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper-white` | Dropdown menu panels, product mockup windows and CTA label text (estimated from screenshots). The one surface brighter than the canvas, so anything on it reads as lifted. |
| Cream Tile | `#f9f7f6` | `--color-cream-tile` | Inactive use-case selector cards and recessed tiles (5 uses). It sits one tonal step below the canvas, so tiles read as pressed in rather than raised. |
| Mint Wash | `#f4fbf7` | `--color-mint-wash` | Section-level background tints behind feature mockups (3 uses). It is atmosphere only. Do not use it as a success-state fill. |
| Keylime Wash | `#f6faeb` | `--color-keylime-wash` | The wavy ribbon behind the press-quote row and the green-tinted mockup edges (1 use). A seasonal pastel that warms the page without spending chroma. |
| Peach Wash | `#fff6f0` | `--color-peach-wash` | The SOC2 compliance callout and the peach gradient behind the hero mockup (1 use). It is the tomato's diluted shadow. Do not stack text-heavy cards on it. |
| Charcoal Glass | `#25221ed4` | `--color-charcoal-glass` | The dark secondary button and inverted overlays (2 uses), which composite to #4a4744 on white. It is the same ink at 83% alpha, so even the inverted surface stays in-family. |
| Ink | `#25221e` | `--color-ink` | Headlines, nav links, button labels and card titles (58 uses). A warm brown-black rather than conventional #000000 or slate, which is why the page reads as printed rather than lit. |
| Graphite Caption | `#25221ea8` | `--color-graphite-caption` | Hero subcopy, feature paragraphs and footer links (69 uses, the most-used color). Ink at 66% alpha is the workhorse that sets reading tone across every section. |
| Ash Caption | `#25221e7d` | `--color-ash-caption` | Tertiary metadata and fine print (1 use). Ink at 49% alpha is the floor for legible text. Do not go lighter for anything a user must read. |
| Stone Border | `#25221e2e` | `--color-stone-border` | The footer top rule, the rating-chip outline and the press-quote dividers (6 uses). An 18%-alpha hairline that tints correctly on every wash beneath it. |
| Mist Fill | `#25221e12` | `--color-mist-fill` | Hover fill on ghost nav links and menu items (1 use). Ink at 7% alpha acts as a pencil smudge rather than a highlight. |
| Ember Signal | `#e34432` | `--color-ember-signal` | The "Start for free" buttons in the nav and hero. It is the only saturated UI color, and its rarity is what makes it findable. Do not use it for links, icons or headings. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Graphik — the headline voice, semibold and tightly tracked at 22–55px · `--font-graphik`

- **Substitute:** Inter Tight at 600, Schibsted Grotesk at 600, Hanken Grotesk at 600. Graphik's semibold renders close to its nominal weight, so match the number and do not drop to 500, which reads noticeably thinner at 38px.
- **Weights:** 400, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 16px, 22px, 38px, 44px, 55px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.15, 1.28
- **Letter spacing:** -0.55px at 55px, -0.44px at 44px, -0.19px at 38px, 0 at 22px and 16px
- **Role:** Graphik is reserved for headings and is not used for long-form reading. That is anti-convention for a SaaS site where one family usually does everything. Weight 600 rather than the conventional 700 keeps 55px headlines firm without shouting. The -0.01em tracking at 44–55px tightens the setting without compressing it. The steps 22 → 38 → 44 → 55 do not follow a modular ratio: 38 to 55 is 1.45, closer to a jump than a ladder. That is deliberate, because a section heading should feel a full size class away from a card title.

### Inter — the UI and reading workhorse, set at medium with open tracking · `--font-inter`

- **Substitute:** Inter at the same weights (the hashed family is a self-hosted Inter cut). Otherwise Geist at 500 or Manrope at 500. All three render true to number, so 500 stays 500.
- **Weights:** 400, 475, 500, 600, 625, 700
- **Sizes:** 12px, 13.5px, 14.5px, 15.5px, 17px, 18px, 18.5px, 20.5px
- **Line height:** 1.35, 1.4, 1.5, 1.6, 1.75
- **Letter spacing:** 0.3px at 12px, 0.135px at 13.5px, 0.18px at 14.5px, 0.155px at 15.5px, 0.17px at 17px, 0.09px at 18px, 0.185px at 18.5px, 0 at 20.5px
- **Role:** Inter at 500 is the default, with 78 uses against 8 at 400. That inverts the convention of 400 body text and gives every label a slightly inked, confident stroke. The variable-axis weights 475 and 625 are intentional half-steps for subcopy and captions. Half-pixel sizes (15.5, 14.5, 20.5) show a scale tuned by eye rather than snapped to integers. Positive +0.01em tracking opens small text the way a book designer loosens captions. The 15.5 → 20.5 step is 1.32, a near Perfect Fourth.

### Caecilia — a slab serif reserved for press quotations · `--font-caecilia`

- **Substitute:** Zilla Slab at 400 italic, Bitter at 400 italic. Caecilia's italic is light-stroked, so do not use 500.
- **Weights:** 400
- **Sizes:** 20px
- **Line height:** 1.8
- **Letter spacing:** 0 at 20px
- **Role:** Caecilia appears 3 times, only on the press quotes from The Verge, PC Mag and TechRadar. The slab italic marks borrowed voices as quoted print and separates them from Todoist's own sans-serif voice. The airy 1.8 line height turns each quote into a pull-quote rather than a testimonial card, which runs against the convention of carded reviews.

A fourth face, Shantell Sans, appears once as a hand-lettered "Take a peek!" annotation. It is decorative and not a system token.

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Inter | 500 | 12px | 1.5 | 0.3px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Inter | 625 | 13.5px | 1.35 | 0.135px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Inter | 400 | 14.5px | 1.5 | 0.18px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Inter | 500 | 15.5px | 1.35 | 0.155px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Inter | 500 | 18px | 1.75 | 0.09px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Inter | 500 | 20.5px | 1.6 | 0px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Graphik | 600 | 22px | 1.28 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Graphik | 600 | 38px | 1.28 | -0.19px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | Graphik | 600 | 44px | 1.15 | -0.44px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | Graphik | 600 | 55px | 1.15 | -0.55px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Derive every neutral from #25221e at alpha: 100% for headings, 66% (#25221ea8) for body, 49% (#25221e7d) for fine print, 18% (#25221e2e) for rules — one ink keeps every wash and surface tonally coherent.
- Reserve #e34432 for "Start for free" and its equivalents, one instance per viewport — the CTA is findable because nothing else on the page is saturated.
- Set headlines in Graphik at 600 with -0.01em tracking (-0.55px at 55px) — semibold at display size reads authoritative without the shout of a 700 or 800 hero.
- Default UI and body text to Inter 500 with +0.01em tracking (0.155px at 15.5px) — the medium stroke gives labels a printed density at small sizes.
- Use 8px radius for nav-level controls and 15px for cards, frames and hero buttons — two radii carry the whole hierarchy of small versus significant.
- Separate feature sections with 128px of #fefdfc canvas and no dividers — whitespace does the sectioning, so hairlines stay rare and meaningful.
- Warm every shadow, using peach rgba(250, 232, 214, 0.6) glows or ink-based rgba(37, 34, 30, 0.18) — elevation should feel like sunlight on paper, not a gray drop.

### Don't

- Don't introduce an opaque gray ramp such as #666666 or #e5e5e5 (not system tokens) — the alpha-ink discipline is non-negotiable, and an opaque gray reads cold against the warm washes.
- Don't color links, icons or eyebrows with #e34432 by default — spending the tomato on decoration turns the CTA into one red item among many.
- Don't set headlines at 700 or 800 in Graphik — the 600 weight at 38–55px is what keeps the hero calm, and bolder weights make it read as a marketing poster.
- Don't drop body text to Inter 400 at 15.5px — on #fefdfc with 66% alpha ink, the lighter stroke loses contrast and the page goes thin.
- Don't wrap feature copy in cards with #f9f7f6 fills and 24px padding — the feature blocks are open text on canvas, and carding them turns a notebook into a dashboard.
- Don't use pill radii of 9999px on buttons — the system tops out at 15px, and pills would read as consumer-playful rather than calm-tool.
- Don't stack the lg shadow onto static cards — it is reserved for floating menus and the dark button, and it should never appear on content at rest.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #fefdfc (Linen Canvas)
- elevated surface: #ffffff (Paper White)
- recessed tile: #f9f7f6 (Cream Tile)
- primary text: #25221e (Ink)
- secondary text: #25221ea8 (Graphite Caption)
- hairline: #25221e2e (Stone Border)
- primary action: #e34432 (filled action)

**Color in Data**

Charts and progress bars draw in ink tints (#25221e12 tracks, #25221e2e gridlines, #25221ea8 series) with #e34432 allowed as one solid highlight series only, and pastel washes reserved for panel backgrounds, so the tomato is never outnumbered by its own data.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a primary action button labeled "Start for free". Use background #e34432, text #ffffff, no border, border-radius 15px, padding 20px 24px, font Inter 18.5px weight 600 with line height 1.4 and letter spacing 0.185px, and no box-shadow. On hover, keep the fill and add `rgba(37, 34, 30, 0.04) 0px 1px 0px 0px`. Make a compact nav variant with border-radius 8px, padding 9px 14px, height 39px, and Inter 15.5px weight 500 with 0.155px letter spacing.

2. Build a navigation bar 72px tall with position static and a transparent background on a #fefdfc page, inner max-width 1312px, centered. On the left place a 128px-wide logo, a 1px #25221e2e vertical divider 24px tall with 16px margins, then the links "Individual", "Business", "Integrations & AI", "Resources" and "Pricing". Each link is #25221e Inter 15.5px weight 500 with 0.155px letter spacing, padding 9px 14px, border-radius 8px, and hover background #25221e12, with a 4px gap between links. On the right place a "Log in" link in the same style and a compact #e34432 button with #ffffff text, 8px radius and 9px 14px padding, 8px apart.

3. Build a hero section on #fefdfc with a 1312px container and two columns at a 48px gap. In the left column put an H1 "Clarity, finally." in Graphik 55px weight 600, line height 1.15, letter spacing -0.55px, color #25221e. Add a 24px gap, then a paragraph in Inter 20.5px weight 500, line height 1.6, color #25221ea8, max-width 500px. Add a 16px gap, then a rating chip with a 1px #25221e2e border, 8px radius, 4px 8px segments and Inter 13.5px weight 625 in #25221ea8. Add a 32px gap, then the primary button from prompt 1. In the right column put a frame with border-radius 15px, a 1px #25221e2e border, a linear gradient from #fff6f0 to #fefdfc, and box-shadow `rgba(42, 29, 48, 0.06) 0px 1px 19px 0px, rgba(250, 232, 214, 0.6) 0px 0px 48px 0px`, containing a #ffffff app screenshot with 10px top corners.

4. Build a feature text block, 500px wide, with no background. Start with an eyebrow in Inter 15.5px weight 600 with 0.155px letter spacing in a decorative section tint. Add a 12px gap, then an H2 in Graphik 38px weight 600, line height 1.28, letter spacing -0.19px, color #25221e. Add a 24px gap, then a paragraph in Inter 18px weight 500, line height 1.75, letter spacing 0.09px, color #25221ea8. Stack blocks 128px apart. Optionally add a callout below at a 32px gap: background #fff6f0, border-radius 10px, padding 12px, a title in Inter 14.5px weight 600 #25221e, and body in Inter 12px weight 500 #25221ea8.

5. Build a dropdown menu panel with background #ffffff, a 1px #25221e2e border, border-radius 13px, padding 4px, width 267px, and box-shadow `rgba(37, 34, 30, 0.07) 0px 14px 19px -9px, rgba(37, 34, 30, 0.18) 0px 10px 48px 0px`. Each item is 43px tall with padding 9px 12px and border-radius 8px. Each has a 16px line icon in #25221ea8 and a 12px gap to a label in Inter 15.5px weight 500 #25221e, with hover background #25221e12.

The only colored control. The hero variant uses background #e34432 with text #ffffff, no border, border-radius 15px and padding 20px 24px (estimated). The nav variant shrinks to 8px radius, 9px 14px padding and 39px height in Inter 15.5px at 500. One tomato per viewport is the rule — it marks the exit, never the decor.

Inverted, in the same ink. Background #25221ed4 (which composites to #4a4744), text #ffffff, no border, border-radius 15px, padding 20px 24px (estimated), Inter 18.5px at 600. Transparent and quiet. **Role:** Static brand and menu header

A filled-free header strip. It sits transparent on #fefdfc, is 72px tall, uses static positioning rather than sticky, and is constrained to 1312px. **Role:** Inline footer announcement tag

A tiny bordered label. It has a transparent background and inherits #25221e text. ## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Derive every neutral from #25221e at alpha: 100% for headings, 66% (#25221ea8) for body, 49% (#25221e7d) for fine print, 18% (#25221e2e) for rules — one ink keeps every wash and surface tonally coherent.
- Reserve #e34432 for "Start for free" and its equivalents, one instance per viewport — the CTA is findable because nothing else on the page is saturated.
- Set headlines in Graphik at 600 with -0.01em tracking (-0.55px at 55px) — semibold at display size reads authoritative without the shout of a 700 or 800 hero.
- Default UI and body text to Inter 500 with +0.01em tracking (0.155px at 15.5px) — the medium stroke gives labels a printed density at small sizes.
- Use 8px radius for nav-level controls and 15px for cards, frames and hero buttons — two radii carry the whole hierarchy of small versus significant.
- Separate feature sections with 128px of #fefdfc canvas and no dividers — whitespace does the sectioning, so hairlines stay rare and meaningful.
- Warm every shadow, using peach rgba(250, 232, 214, 0.6) glows or ink-based rgba(37, 34, 30, 0.18) — elevation should feel like sunlight on paper, not a gray drop.

### Don't

- Don't introduce an opaque gray ramp such as #666666 or #e5e5e5 (not system tokens) — the alpha-ink discipline is non-negotiable, and an opaque gray reads cold against the warm washes.
- Don't color links, icons or eyebrows with #e34432 by default — spending the tomato on decoration turns the CTA into one red item among many.
- Don't set headlines at 700 or 800 in Graphik — the 600 weight at 38–55px is what keeps the hero calm, and bolder weights make it read as a marketing poster.
- Don't drop body text to Inter 400 at 15.5px — on #fefdfc with 66% alpha ink, the lighter stroke loses contrast and the page goes thin.
- Don't wrap feature copy in cards with #f9f7f6 fills and 24px padding — the feature blocks are open text on canvas, and carding them turns a notebook into a dashboard.
- Don't use pill radii of 9999px on buttons — the system tops out at 15px, and pills would read as consumer-playful rather than calm-tool.
- Don't stack the lg shadow onto static cards — it is reserved for floating menus and the dark button, and it should never appear on content at rest.

## Imagery

Imagery is product UI first. The hero shows a desktop Todoist window with a phone overlapping its right edge. Feature sections show cropped app panels with sidebars, project lists and colored # hashtags. Frames take 15px outer radius, a 1px #25221e2e hairline, and the peach md glow on a #fff6f0-to-#fefdfc gradient. Inner windows are #ffffff with 10px top-only corners. Text inside mockups is often replaced by rounded skeleton bars, so the UI illustrates the idea without inviting a close read. Icons are 16px single-weight line glyphs in #25221ea8. Decorative illustration is limited to the press-quote ribbon: yellow four-point sparkles, orange dots, a coral plus and green check circles floating on a #f6faeb wave. These are decorative, not tokens. There is no photography and no glowing orb. The narrative is that the product itself is the picture.

## Layout

Content sits in a 1312px container inside a 1360px outer frame. Feature text columns narrow to 500px. Sections are separated by 128px of bare canvas, with 96px on tighter transitions. The hero is a two-column split. On the left are the 55px display headline, 20.5px subcopy, the rating chip and the tomato CTA. On the right, the product mockup frame takes about 55% of the width. Below it, a full-bleed press-quote ribbon runs three columns. Feature blocks alternate text left with a sticky mockup right, and each block is introduced by a tinted eyebrow. The use-case selector runs as a horizontal row of six tiles. The nav is static, transparent and 72px tall, with the logo and five links on the left and "Log in" plus the CTA on the right. The footer is a hairline-topped multi-column sitemap. At 375px, use the 38px heading size for the H1, collapse to one column, and use 64px section gaps. Overall density: spacious.

## Alpha Ink Discipline

The defining move is that Todoist owns one neutral, #25221e, and expresses every gray as that ink at a fixed alpha: 100% for headings, 66% for body, 49% for fine print, 18% for rules and 7% for hover. Even the dark secondary button is 83% ink. This differs from the conventional 50-to-900 gray ramp, and it means every text color and hairline inherits the warmth of whatever wash it sits on. The discipline breaks the moment someone hard-codes an opaque #666666 or a cool slate border (neither is a system token). That color reads blue-gray against #fff6f0 and #f6faeb, and the paper illusion collapses. To extend the system, pick a new alpha stop on the same ink, such as a pressed state. Do not pick a new hex.

## Rationed Tomato Accent

The chromatic budget is exactly one saturated hue: #e34432, spent on the "Start for free" action in the nav and hero. Everything else that looks colorful is either a pastel wash (#f4fbf7, #f6faeb, #fff6f0), a decorative eyebrow tint or the illustration confetti, and none of it is a system token for interaction. That is stricter than the typical SaaS habit of coloring links, icons, focus rings and badges with the brand color. The rule breaks when tomato leaks onto secondary buttons, link text or chart fills, because the user then loses the single place to click. Extend it by adding new states to the existing button, such as hover or loading. A new feature needing emphasis gets a wash or a 600 weight, not red.

## Similar Brands

- **Notion** — It shares a warm off-white canvas and brown-black ink instead of pure #000000, but Notion leans on black buttons where Todoist spends one tomato.
- **Things (Cultured Code)** — It shares the calm task-manager stance and product-screenshot-as-hero composition, with a cooler blue accent rationed just as tightly.
- **Asana** — It is a direct category competitor with a coral-red brand, but Asana spreads that hue across gradients and illustration, while Todoist confines it to the CTA.
- **Basecamp** — It shares the editorial, document-like scroll with static navigation and generous section gaps, though it uses heavier type and louder yellow highlights.
- **Twist** — The same parent company, with the same Graphik-plus-Inter pairing, pastel washes and soft 8–15px radii, applied to messaging instead of tasks.
